title: Refuse queued requests lacking bullets, files, or job-id dependencies
summary: `athena ask --later` will check the request text against the parse `athena plan` uses (bullet acceptance, path-like file words, full job ids for dependencies) and refuse with a message naming the missing part, recording nothing. Audience: operators queueing requests. Assumption: a dependency is only "missing" when the text says it depends on or comes after another job ("after", "depends on", "retry of", "blocked by") but names no full job id; requests that state no dependency are not refused for that.

defaults_applied.how: Three new tests plus a passing queued case; cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria check refusals and acceptance by running tests.
Refuse at queue time using the same parse as plan, rather than closing requests later.
One focused validator plus its call site.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The check applies only to the user-facing `athena ask --later` path (main.rs), because internal callers and many existing tests queue unstructured text.
A request with no stated dependency is not refused for lacking one; only a dependency phrase without a full job id is.
The validation function lives in reading.rs next to the plan parse helpers; the refusal text names the missing part (acceptance, files, or job id).

acceptance_criteria.text: Test: a request with files and no `-`/`*`/numbered bullets is refused with an error naming the missing acceptance bullets, and no records commit is made. Run `cargo test`.
Test: a request with bullets and no path-like word is refused with an error naming the missing files. Run `cargo test`.

Test: a request with bullets and files that says it comes 'after' another job without a full job id is refused with an error naming the missing job id; and a request with bullets, files and a valid full job id is queued. Run `cargo test`.

Existing tests that call `Athena::queue` with free text (code_health, hestia, drain, lifecycle) still pass, so the check applies at the `ask --later` entry (or a separate checked method), not to internal queuing. Run `cargo test`.
The check reuses `request_text_acceptance`, `request_text_touches` and `job_ids_in` in reading.rs so it cannot drift from the `athena plan` parse.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Validating requests queued internally by code_health, hestia or steward
departures: Ambiguity about whether dependencies are mandatory and where to apply the check raises intervention risk slightly.
